citation: Rose, J., Thomas, S., Zhang, L., Edwards, A., Augero, A., & Roney, P. (2017). Research Learning Communities: Evaluation report and executive summary. London: Education Endowment Foundation. (Independent evaluation, University of Bristol; intervention delivered by UCL Institute of Education, led by Dr Chris Brown.)
report_number: EEF project: Research Learning Communities (RLC); ERIC ED581267; trial registration ISRCTN14382473
design: Two-armed cluster RCT (efficacy trial; unit of randomisation = school, with some schools randomised in federation/alliance units via minimisation on size, %FSM and KS2 attainment); 119 primary schools recruited and randomised (60 intervention / 59 control; 71 randomisation units), reducing to 116 schools (59 intervention; 57 control) at analysis; 5,462 pupils at randomisation. TPD intervention = Research Learning Communities: two 'Evidence Champion' teachers per school attended 4 workshops/year over two academic years (Oct 2014-June 2016), developed/delivered by UCL IOE academics, then led school/key-stage improvement strategies based on engaging with research evidence. Business-as-usual control (£1,000 incentive for full participation). Outcomes = Year 6 KS2 attainment (the 2014/15 Year 5 ITT cohort, tested at KS2 in 2015/16) from the National Pupil Database. Primary outcome = KS2 Reading; secondary outcomes = KS2 Numeracy (maths) and KS2 Grammar, Punctuation & Spelling (GPS). Population: English primary schools, slightly above-average disadvantage (14.1% FSM, sample mean ~20-22% FSM). EEF security rating for the primary outcome: 5/5 padlocks (very high).
problems: All extracted effect sizes are the EEF-reported standardized effect sizes from the report's Tables 6 (primary outcome) and 7 (secondary outcomes), computed per EEF guidance as ES = (treatment-group coefficient from the final multilevel model) / sqrt(total variance after controls), using the random-part estimate from the final pupil-level multilevel model (Stata). These are cluster-adjusted (3-level random part: school + pupil; clustering of schools within RLCs was tested but not retained as it confounded with treatment/control coding) and pretest/covariate-adjusted (standardized KS1 reading/writing/maths/science scores, everFSM, school FSM%, school average KS2, school size, randomisation control variables). The report labels these 'effect size'; it does not print the small-sample J multiplier, but with df in the thousands J~1 so the reported ES ~ Hedges g. The report does NOT print impact-estimate standard errors directly on the ES scale; g_se/g_var here are derived from the reported 95% confidence intervals (CI = fixed-part treatment estimate +/- 1.96 SD, per the report's stated effect-size method). The Appendix H model-3 treatment coefficients (KS2 Reading b=0.02 SE 0.05; KS2 Numeracy b=0.04 SE 0.06; KS2 GPS b=0.07 SE 0.06) are rounded to 2 dp and do not exactly reproduce the Table 6/7 ES (the ES were computed from unrounded model output); the Table 6/7 ES are the authoritative reported values and are used as g, with the model coefficients/variance components recorded in g_method/notes. ICC recorded (0.11) is the analysis-stage design-effect ICC from Table 4. NOTE on registry coding: the meta-analysis registry lists TPD Trainer = 'Res/Dev' (the PD was developer/researcher-delivered by UCL IOE academics), NOT a description of the test; the achievement tests are National Curriculum KS2 assessments obtained from the National Pupil Database, i.e. externally set/marked standardized independent measures -> test_type=standardized_independent. KS2 Writing was available (teacher-assessed) but the evaluators deliberately did not use it due to low correlation with other KS2 measures (not extracted; never reported as an impact). FSM-pupil subgroup rows are extracted for completeness with is_full_sample=false / outcome_role=subgroup (these are non-randomised subsets); literacy-focus and numeracy-focus school subgroup rows are NOT extracted (they are overlapping reanalyses of the same full sample split by Y1 workshop focus, not pupil subgroups, and would double-count the full-sample contrasts). For the meta-analysis the qualifying TPD-vs-control STUDENT-achievement full-sample contrasts are: KS2 Reading (Reading, primary, g=0.02), KS2 Numeracy (STEM, secondary, g=0.06), KS2 GPS (Other, secondary, g=0.10).

effect_sizes.arm_label: Research Learning Communities (single TPD arm) vs business-as-usual control
effect_sizes.test_name: KS2 Reading (National Curriculum test, 2015/16, via National Pupil Database; standardized score)
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (KS2 May 2016, end of 2-year intervention; 2014/15 Year 5 ITT cohort tested at KS2 in Year 6 2015/16)
effect_sizes.g_method: EEF cluster-randomised standardized effect size = (final-model treatment coefficient) / sqrt(total variance after controls), from a 3-level multilevel model (school + pupil random part) in Stata, controlling for standardized KS1 reading/writing/maths/science, everFSM, school FSM%, school average KS2, school size and randomisation variables. g = reported ES from Table 6 = 0.02. Appendix H Table H.1 (model 3): treatment b=0.02 (SE 0.05); random part school variance 0.06, student variance 0.47 (total 0.53), N=4966, 116 groups. g_se/g_var derived from reported 95% CI (-0.09, 0.12): SE = 0.21/(2*1.96) = 0.0536, g_var = 0.002872. df in thousands so J~1, g~d.
